newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA MULLS $60 MLN FUND FOR WHEAT IMPORTS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA MULLS $60 MLN FUND FOR WHEAT IMPORTS.

text.p: Romania plans to use a first tranche of World Bank loans to set up a hard currency fund of around $60 million for wheat imports in case of emergency, the agriculture minister said on Friday.
"We intend to create a hard-currency fund for wheat imports to complete the country's reserves if the situation requires that," Dinu Gavrilescu told a news conference after Friday's cabinet meeting.
The fund would be financed with money from a first tranche of an ASAL (Agricultural Structural Adjustment Loan) deal agreed with the World Bank, expected to come in July, he said.
Earlier this week the agriculture ministry said some 550,000 tonnes of wheat would be taken out from the country's strategic reserves to ensure flour supplies to bakeries.

Romania, which exported wheat last year, might resort to imports in the first half of 1997, to compensate for a wheat shortage following last year's poor crop, ministry officials said, declining to give an amount for the planned imports.
Romania had 2.11 million of hectares under wheat in 1996, when a bad winter damaged the crop on half that area.
Last year Romania harvested less than 60 percent of its bumper crop of some 7.8 million tonnes in 1995, when exports amounted to 1.3 million tonnes.
Ministry data show that wheat was sown on 2.1 million hectares last autumn, and that the country expects a wheat crop of around 6.0 million tonnes this year. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
